 Overseas Update: Usama shows class whilst Women’s Rapids duo shine down under
 Published 19/11/2026 
 All News 
 Club News 
 First Team 
 Women's Rapids 
 Player News 
 Second Team 
 Academy 
 In another week where Worcestershire Men’s and Women’s stars showed their skills across the globe, there were highlights from Australia, Nepal, South Africa and the West Indies.
 Usama Mir sparkled on debut for Chitwan Rhinos, there was a welcome return to action for recently re-signed youngster Dan Lategan at home in Cape Town, and Women’s Rapids pair Madison Windeatt and Amy Maund began their overseas adventure.
 Adam Finch: England Lions
 Having starred in the opening One Day fixture of a five-match series against West Indies, Adam was rested for the following game, watching on as his team secured a dominant 276-run victory.
 Reintroduced to the XI for the third match, Adam produced another economical spell with the ball, returning figures of 2-39 as England Lions chased down 274 with six-wickets in hand.
 Although going wicketless in the fourth match of the tour, the Worcestershire seamer did chip in with 11 runs in England Lions’ total of 330, which eventually proved 80-runs too many for the hosts.
 Having been rested for the final match of the series, Adam’s attentions now turn to a three match One Day series against South Africa A at the start of next month.
 Usama Mir: Nepal T20
 After watching his side seal a four wicket win over Janakpur Bolts, Usama made his tournament bow for the Rhinos in style a two days later.
 Despite taking 2-31 with the ball and producing a swashbuckling late 28 from 23 balls, Usama couldn’t stop the Rhinos from falling 24 runs short in their chase of 154 to beat the Kanarli Yarks.
 Having qualified for the playoffs, Usama showed his white ball class once more in a commanding 61-run victory over Kathmandu Gurkhas, spinning his way to figures of 3-15 as the Rhinos skittled their opponents for just 143 in reply to their first innings 204-4.
 The Rhinos will now face Sudurpaschim Royals in the second play-off fixture later this week.
 Henry Cullen: Woodville CC – Australia
 After making a similarly positive start last weekend against Tea Tree Gully, Henry made 15 from 18 balls but couldn’t prevent his side from falling to a heavy 135 run defeat as they were bowled out for 229 in pursuit of 364-9d.
 Madison Windeatt: Croydon Ranges CC – Australia
 It has been a stellar start to the Australian summer for young Rapids star Madison, who has laced 177 runs in her first five appearances for new side Croydon Ranges in Victoria.
 In her opening T20 fixture against Lyndale/CUCC the top-order batter smashed 64 from just 46 balls with six fours as she propelled her side to a 60-run victory.
 A duck followed on her fifty over debut, but the starlet hit back with a composed run-a-ball 22 for the senior Women’s side against Montrose Women during a One Day defeat, but the excellent form continued.
 41 from 40 balls opening the batting for the 1 st XI helped Croydon Ranges to a 21-run win over North Ringwood women, before a second half century of the season followed in a match-winning second wicket stand of 108 in the nine-wicket thumping of Wandin Women.
 Brett D’Oliveira: Green Point CC – South Africa
 There was a welcome return to action for the Worcestershire skipper over the weekend, with the middle-order batter starring for his adopted side in a seven wicket win over Breckenfell CC in the Western Province Club Premier League.
 Set 191 to win, Brett came in at number four to ease his side to victory with a stylish 41 not-out from 43 balls.
 Dan Lategan: Durbanville CC – South Africa
 Having signed his new deal at the Club this week, Pear’s prodigy Dan made a perfect start to his winter back home for boyhood outfit Durbanville CC.
 In a thumping 128-run win, the 20-year-old number three made a superb 57 from 69 deliveries including six-fours and two-sixes as the hosts posted 284-7, restricting Claremont CC to just 156 all-out in reply.
